title: A second life for the school courtyard
paragraphs: For years, a concrete courtyard beside Meranti Secondary School became almost unusable after heavy rain. Water spread across the lowest corner, while the bare surface grew uncomfortably hot on clear afternoons. Most students crossed the area quickly instead of spending time there.

The science club decided to study the problem before suggesting a solution. Members measured where water collected and compared surface temperatures at different times of day. They proposed a rain garden: several shallow beds filled with soil and native plants. Rather than sending all the rain directly into drains, the beds would retain some of it around their roots.

At first, the new garden looked unremarkable. Then a strong storm filled the shallow beds without flooding the walkway. Within a few hours, the soil had absorbed the pooled water. This result persuaded the school to add two more beds near the canteen.

A year later, teachers sometimes hold short lessons in the cooler courtyard. Butterflies visit the flowering plants, and students record changes in the garden after each storm. The project was modest, but it changed how the school community viewed an overlooked space: the courtyard could manage rain, support wildlife and still remain useful to people.
